newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CSR sees few Australia investment plans.
newsitem.headline: CSR sees few Australia investment plans.

text.p: CSR Ltd said on Monday that it did not expect to make further significant investment in its construction and building materials business in Australia due to the subdued outlook for the industry.
CSR, one of Australia's biggest building materials suppliers, has spent over A$2.0 billion over the past four years on its operations in Asia, Australia and the United States.

"As to Australia, we do see very little opportunity," managing director Geoff Kells told reporters after CSR announced a 36 percent drop in net profit after abnormals to A$212.2 million for the year to March 31, 1997.
"We do see continuing growth opportunities in America, that is what we have been doing and specific add-on opportunities will be sought in Asia," Kells said.
Kells said the company's A$2.0 billion capital expenditure programme was largely over and that the company would have to start improving its returns from existing assets.
The 1996/97 year profit reflected a return of 7.9 percent on funds employed before abnormal items, its worst performance in four years. CSR has over A$7.79 billion in assets.
"We accept that the profit performance is totally inadequate," Kells said.
CSR earlier blamed the 1996/97 profit drop on the downturn in the domestic housing market, which is due to turn around in the 1997/98 year and improve the company's profit.
CSR shares closed 0.7 cents down at A$4.763.
